name: NocoDB Cloud
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Use a managed spreadsheet interface over structured data

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 3 editors and 10 commenters; 1,000 records; 1 GB storage; 100 automation runs/month; 1,000 API calls/month; 1 extension; 0 external database connections.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 50,000 records; 20 GB storage; 100,000 API calls/month; 30-day revision history; 2 snapshots; 0 external database connections.
tiers.notes: The live plan card says 10,000 automation runs, while the live comparison table says 30,000. Seat charges are capped after 9 paid users.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 300,000 records; 100 GB storage; 1 million API calls/month; 10 external database connections; 90-day history; 5 snapshots.
tiers.notes: The live plan card says 50,000 automation runs, while the live comparison table says 120,000. Seat charges are capped after 9 paid users.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: 1 million records; 150 GB storage; 5 million API calls/month; 180-day history; 10 snapshots.
tiers.notes: The live page conflicts with itself: it says both 'no seat minimums' and a 3-seat minimum, and shows 250,000 automation runs on the card versus 240,000 in the table.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited records; 1 TB storage; 365+ days of history; 50+ snapshots; custom usage and security limits.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 editors, 10 commenters, 1,000 records, 1 GB storage, 100 automation runs/month, 1,000 API calls/month, 1 extension and no external database connections
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; published annual rates are 20% lower
pricing.hiddenCosts: Plus and Business billing is capped at 9 paid seats ($135/$270 monthly or $108/$216 annual-equivalent); Scale has contradictory 0-versus-3-seat-minimum language; overage rates are not published, so higher usage may require an upgrade.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For NocoDB Cloud, use a managed spreadsheet interface over structured data. The hard boundary is managed hosting, integrations, collaboration, storage, and support, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Model structured records behind a spreadsheet-style interface, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: managed hosting, integrations, collaboration, storage, and support
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for NocoDB Cloud because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: Airtable with fewer ornaments: 3,000 rows, forms, views, automations, and a small app builder for $0.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Baserow Free primarily stores data in its own database instead of providing NocoDB's direct spreadsheet-style layer over an existing SQL schema.

alternatives.name: Grist
alternatives.desc: Self-hosted rather than managed, but a polished relational grid with formulas and forms.

facts.install: Hosted signup, desktop app, or Docker container for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Each document is a .grist SQLite database containing table data, attachments, document metadata, and recent history; CSV/Excel exports are also available
facts.gapVsPaid: Grist is a relational spreadsheet document rather than a live administrative facade over existing databases, and shared use usually adds self-hosting work.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted or desktop use; shared self-hosting requires Docker, authentication, backups, a public URL, and safe Python-formula sandboxing

alternatives.name: NocoDB Free
alternatives.desc: The same managed product: three editors, 1,000 records, forms, grid, kanban, gallery, webhooks, and API access.

facts.dataFormat: Free-plan records and attachments live in NocoDB Cloud; records can be exported through the UI/API, but external database connections are not included on the free plan
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same cloud product, but the free workspace's record, editor, storage, and automation limits are too small for many paid NocoDB deployments.

alternatives.name: SeaTable Free
alternatives.desc: A serious grid with 10,000 rows, forms, automations, scripts, and an app builder before it asks for money.

facts.dataFormat: Bases live in SeaTable Cloud and can be exported as proprietary .dtable containers containing JSON plus an asset folder; individual tables or views export to XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: SeaTable keeps records inside its own base format and does not replace NocoDB's core strength of exposing an existing SQL database through a grid and API.

alternatives.name: Teable Free
alternatives.desc: An Airtable-shaped database with 1,000 rows, 100 automations, and a real app builder on the free plan.

facts.engines: Vendor-hosted AI and App Builder features use Teable's configured model services and free-plan credits; the exact model roster can change
facts.dataFormat: Bases, records, attachments, automation state, and app definitions live in Teable Cloud; bases can be backed up as .tea files and tables exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable is an excellent hosted base, but it is not a drop-in live interface over arbitrary existing SQL schemas in the way paid NocoDB can be.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for NocoDB Cloud in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records behind a spreadsheet-style interface, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
